title: The Wobbly Duck Sign
markdown:
The sunbeams stretched across the meadow, waking Edie the dormouse in her cozy burrow. “What a lovely day for friends!” she thought.

Soon, a cheerful oink-snuffle announced Pearl the piglet, her nose dusted with yellow pollen. Miss Clover, with her soft ears, hopped over. “Hello, friends!” she whispered. “This meadow is so sunny!”

“It feels like a day for something special!” Edie chirped.

Suddenly, happy quacks filled the air! Mrs Puddles the duck waddled in with her seven fluffy ducklings. Pip, the smallest, tumbled but bounced right up with a happy peep! “Look!” quacked Mrs Puddles. “Mr Diggle made us a sign!”

Near the pond, a new sign stood, painted in big, blue letters: MIND THE DUCKS.

“For us?” chirped Pip. “He wrote it just for us!” quacked Dottie. Mrs Puddles puffed out her chest. “Of course! We are very important ducks!”

Edie, Pearl, and Miss Clover smiled. They knew the sign was for everyone to be careful of the ducks. But it was sweet how special the ducks felt.

“Let’s go see the important sign!” squealed Pearl, trotting towards the pond. Edie and Miss Clover followed, their paws making soft pitter-patter sounds.

“It is a very important sign,” whispered Miss Clover. “Mr Diggle always does a wonderful job.”

Pearl nudged her backpack. “I brought berry sandwiches for everyone!” she announced. She spread out a picnic blanket. Soon, yummy sandwiches and dandelions lay before them. The ducklings pecked happily.

“This is more fun than just thinking about being careful,” quacked Pip. “It’s fun to be minded! It feels like everyone cares!”

The sun shone, the sandwiches were yummy, and the ducks felt like the most important residents. They even did a little waddle-dance around the sign, their webbed feet tapping a happy rhythm.

Then, a gentle gust of wind sighed through the trees. Whooosh. The sign wobbled. Wibble-wobble. It swayed like it was dancing.

The ducks stopped. “Oh dear!” quacked Mrs Puddles. “Is it going to fall?”

The sign tilted. Thump! It landed on its side in the grass.

A hush fell. Pip’s lip trembled. He felt a little sad. “The sign… it’s not there anymore,” he whispered. “Nobody will mind us now.”

Edie’s whiskers drooped. Pearl’s smile wavered. The ducks’ special importance seemed to have disappeared. They sat in a quiet circle, the fallen sign looking forgotten.

Just then, cheerful whistling echoed. Whistle, whistle, whirr! Mr Diggle the badger bustled into view, a shiny trowel in his paw. “Hello, everyone!” he boomed. He spotted the sign. “Oh, dear me! A bit of wind, I suppose? That won’t do at all!”

The ducks looked up hopefully. Mr Diggle gently picked up the sign. “This sign is very important,” he said, kind and firm. “And it’s important for everyone to see it. Especially our wonderful, deserving ducks!” He winked at Mrs Puddles.

Edie, Pearl, and Miss Clover scurried over. “We can help!” chirped Edie. “I can hold it steady!” squeaked Pearl. “I can help dig the hole deeper,” offered Miss Clover.

Together, the badger, the dormouse, the piglet, and the rabbit worked as a team. Mr Diggle pushed the sign back into the ground. Pearl held it straight. Miss Clover packed the soil tight. The ducks watched, their heads bobbing, quacking little words of encouragement.

Mr Diggle patted the ground one last time. The sign stood tall and strong. It said: MIND THE DUCKS. It looked even better!

The ducks let out a joyful QUACK! QUACK! QUACK! Pip flapped his wings, giggling. Mrs Puddles beamed. “Thank you, Mr Diggle! And thank you, dear friends!” she quacked.

Edie smiled, her whiskers twitching happily. Pearl offered a last crumb. The meadow felt even safer and brighter, with the sign standing tall and the ducks still dancing, just a little, around its feet.
characters: Edie (a dormouse), Pearl (a piglet), Clover (a rabbit)
author: StoryGen Community
